excerpt: Raycast is a keyboard launcher with extensions, clipboard history, snippets and built-in AI, for Mac, Windows and iOS. Free and paid plans, and alternatives.
content:
Raycast is a launcher: press a keyboard shortcut, type, and open apps, files and commands without reaching for the mouse. It runs on Mac and Windows, and there is an iOS version too. Beyond launching, it bundles several everyday utilities in one app: clipboard history, window management, snippets that expand short keywords into longer text, quicklinks and hotkeys. An Extension Store adds commands for other apps such as Linear, Spotify, Slack and Notion, so you can act in them from the launcher, and developers can build and publish their own extensions. Raycast AI brings chat and AI commands into the same window and works with the tools you already use.

Raycast's homepage cites a 99.8% crash-free rate, a Slack community of 37,000 members and 90,000 followers on X. It does not publish user numbers or funding on the pages we checked.

Free and paid plans

The core launcher is free. The Free plan includes the core features, thousands of extensions, custom extensions and developer tools, three months of clipboard history and five notes, but no Raycast AI. Paid plans for individuals add AI and are sold in three sizes that differ mainly in AI credits and model access. Pro costs $10 a month or $96 a year with 500 AI credits a month, bring-your-own-key support, cloud sync, dictation, custom themes, a translator and unlimited clipboard history and notes, but not the top-tier AI models. Plus costs $20 a month ($192 a year) with 3,000 credits and top-tier models, and Max $50 a month ($480 a year) with 7,500 credits.

Teams pay per user: Teams Free costs nothing and allows shared commands, quicklinks and snippets within limits; Teams Pro is $15 a user a month, Teams Plus $25 and Teams Max $65, mirroring the individual credit levels. Enterprise is custom and adds an AI Control Center (organisation-wide AI switches, approved providers, your own keys) plus SAML, SCIM and other admin controls. AI credits expire 60 days after each monthly grant, and students get 50% off Pro.

We have not tested Raycast ourselves. This page brings together Raycast's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Keyboard launcher with extensions, clipboard history, snippets and built-in AI

use_cases: Open apps, files and system commands from the keyboard
Search clipboard history and paste earlier items
Expand short keywords into full text with snippets
Control apps such as Linear, Slack or Spotify through extensions
Ask an AI model a question without opening a browser (paid plans)

fit: live on the keyboard and want one launcher instead of several small utilities
want AI chat a shortcut away and are happy paying for credits
are a team that wants shared snippets and commands
not_fit: want AI on the free plan: Raycast AI starts with Pro
need top-tier AI models on the $10 Pro plan: they start with Plus
are happy with the launcher built into your operating system

pros: Free plan covers the core launcher and thousands of extensions
Several utilities (clipboard, windows, snippets) in one app
Clear, published prices for individuals and teams
cons: No AI on the free plan
AI credits expire 60 days after each grant
Top-tier AI models need Plus or Max

alternatives.intro: Other keyboard launchers. Descriptions come from each product's own site.

items.name: Alfred
items.what: Productivity app for macOS with hotkeys, keywords, text expansion and custom actions through its Powerpack
items.difference: Mac only; custom workflows come with the paid Powerpack.

items.name: LaunchBar
items.what: Mac launcher that gives keyboard access to every corner of your Mac
items.difference: Long-running Mac launcher without a built-in AI subscription.
